 Twitch launches shoppable and skippable ads as Razer reports 2.44x ROAS
 Twitch adds Amazon shoppable overlays and qualified-view skippable ads, with Razer reporting 2.44x ROAS in a US test.
 Celi Anindia 
 16 Nov 2026 
 • 4 min read 
 ✦

 Get personalised takeaways tailored to your role and goals 
 ↓ 
 Twitch is adding two advertising formats designed to make livestream campaigns easier to connect to sales and meaningful viewer engagement. The Amazon-owned platform introduced shoppable video overlays in a North American desktop beta and plans a self-service skippable ad beta for December 2026.
 The announcement, made around TwitchCon San Diego, is a bid to move Twitch beyond a reach-and-awareness pitch. Shoppable ads connect product discovery to Amazon carts, while skippable ads bill brands for qualified viewing or clicks. Gaming hardware maker Razer's reported test result offers an early performance signal, although it should not be treated as a universal benchmark.
 Table of contents
 Jump to each section:
 How Twitch shoppable ads connect streams to Amazon purchases 
 Skippable ads introduce a qualified-view billing model 
 What Razer's 2.44x ROAS result actually shows 
 Why Amazon wants Twitch to work across the funnel 
 What advertisers should test before scaling 
 Key Takeaways
 Twitch shoppable video overlays entered open desktop beta for US and Canadian advertisers in November 2026.
 A separate skippable ad beta is scheduled for December, with billing tied to qualifying views or clicks.
 Razer's reported 2.44x ROAS is one advertiser's test result, not a platform-wide forecast.
 How Twitch shoppable ads connect streams to Amazon purchases
 Twitch's new shoppable advertising format adds an interactive overlay to video ads. Viewers can explore advertised products, compare available styles and add items to an Amazon cart while watching a livestream. The purchase is completed through Amazon's commerce experience, not through a separate advertiser landing page.
 The format entered an open desktop beta for advertisers in the United States and Canada on November 13, around TwitchCon San Diego. Advertised products must already be listed on Amazon, which reduces the need to create separate product pages or bespoke commerce creative. Buyers can purchase the inventory alongside Prime Video through Amazon Ads Agent.
 The rollout has limits. Twitch plans to extend availability across Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, and Asia Pacific during the first half of 2027. Mobile and connected-TV versions are planned, rather than generally available today.

 A second format gives Twitch advertisers an alternative to paying for every served video impression. Its self-service open beta is scheduled for December 2026. Advertisers pay when a viewer watches more than 30 seconds, completes an ad shorter than that threshold, or clicks.
 That pricing structure makes the format a different proposition from Twitch's existing premium video placements, which Amazon Ads describes as unskippable . For advertisers testing a live-video audience, the appeal is paying for a defined engagement rather than assuming every delivered ad attracted comparable attention.
 It does not eliminate the need for careful measurement. A qualified view is not necessarily an incremental sale, and a click is not proof of purchase. Marketers should compare downstream conversion and customer acquisition costs, not only the number of billable views.
 What Razer's 2.44x ROAS result actually shows
 Gaming hardware brand Razer tested skippable advertising in the United States. In the results shared with Marketing Dive , the campaign produced a return on ad spend about twice that of its previous standard Twitch video campaigns. One-third of customers reached through the skippable campaign were reported as new to the brand.
 2.44x ROAS was reported for Razer's US skippable-ad test, according to the results shared with Marketing Dive. The figure is a single advertiser's campaign result, not an independently established Twitch-wide benchmark.
 The comparison is promising but narrow. The public reporting does not establish a controlled experiment with identical audiences, creative and budgets. The result therefore supports a case for testing the new format, not a forecast of what other advertisers will earn.
 Why Amazon wants Twitch to work across the funnel
 The two launches address different steps in the same advertising journey. Shoppable overlays shorten the path from product discovery to an Amazon purchase. Skippable ads make the cost of reaching an attentive viewer more explicit. Together, they move Twitch's pitch beyond gaming-community awareness toward measurable commercial outcomes.
 The strategy also connects Twitch to Amazon's wider advertising inventory. A brand already selling products through Amazon and advertising on Prime Video can explore another environment without building an entirely separate commerce destination. The trade-off is that the shoppable format depends on Amazon product availability.
 There is a broader shift behind the announcement. The IAB's 2026 outlook study identifies shoppable advertising and ads within live programming among the formats attracting increased buyer attention. Those buyer intentions do not establish that Twitch's new units will convert, but they explain why the platform is prioritizing them.
 In a TwitchCon interview with Net Influencer , Twitch chief product officer Mike Minton described the platform's broader push to help brands connect livestream engagement with commercial outcomes. The new ad units fit that ambition while leaving execution and measurement questions for advertisers to test.
 What advertisers should test before scaling
 Brands with Amazon-listed products can begin by comparing shoppable overlays against existing Twitch or Prime Video creative, measuring cart additions and completed purchases rather than treating interaction alone as a conversion. The beta's desktop-only scope should be accounted for when interpreting results.
 For skippable ads, advertisers should define a qualified-view benchmark, then assess cost per completed view, incremental conversions and new-customer acquisition alongside ROAS. Razer's result provides a reference point for the product's potential, but not a guaranteed return.
 The practical question is whether Twitch's live attention can produce profitable actions without making the viewing experience less appealing. The new formats give advertisers two ways to find out, with important availability and attribution limits still in place.
